qs.q: In a patient with two functioning kidneys, what must occur for urinary tract obstruction to cause postrenal AKI?
o: The obstruction must be bilateral
It must involve the upper ureter only
There must be associated renal dysplasia
It must coincide with acute tubular necrosis
qs.e: In a patient with two functioning kidneys, an obstruction must be bilateral to result in AKI. Unilateral obstruction alone is generally insufficient to cause acute kidney injury if the contralateral kidney functions normally.

qs.q: What is the typical consequence of bilateral lower urinary tract obstruction caused by prostatic nodular hyperplasia?
o: Contralateral renal agenesis
Ureteropelvic junction obstruction
Raised intravesical pressure and hypertrophy
Exstrophy of the bladder
qs.e: Obstruction raises intravesical pressure, which leads to detrusor muscle hypertrophy and can cause acquired bladder diverticula. Prostatic enlargement is a distal obstruction in men rather than a congenital anomaly like UPJ obstruction.

qs.q: What is the primary diagnostic modality used to identify urinary tract obstruction in post-renal azotemia?
o: Non-contrast computed tomography
Intravenous pyelography procedure
Renal ultrasonography procedure
Magnetic resonance angiography
qs.e: Obstruction is usually diagnosed by the presence of ureteral and renal pelvic dilation on renal ultrasound. Post-renal causes account for less than 5% of acute renal failure cases.

qs.q: What is the primary physiological consequence when urinary tract obstruction causes urine to back up into the kidney?
o: Increased pressure destroys kidney tissue over time
Immediate and permanent cessation of filtration
Immediate conversion of nephrons into glomeruli
Alkaline conversion of urine within the cortex
qs.e: Backed-up urine increases pressure inside the kidney, which progressively destroys kidney tissue. Glomerular filtration actually continues for a while before failing.

qs.q: What is the typical presentation of a patient with a unilateral urinary tract obstruction?
o: It can be completely silent because the contralateral kidney compensates
It invariably presents with acute anuria and immediate renal failure
It presents exclusively with severe polyuria and nocturia from day one
It always causes bilateral flank pain and dramatic macroscopic hematuria
qs.e: A unilateral obstruction can remain silent for a long time as the healthy contralateral kidney maintains normal renal function. Complete bilateral obstruction causes oliguria or anuria.

qs.q: What is the characteristic clinical finding in a patient presenting with bilateral partial urinary tract obstruction?
o: Inability to concentrate urine leading to polyuria and nocturia
Massive localized unilateral renal cyst formation up to 20 cm
Immediate complete cessation of all systemic urine output
Exclusive production of alkaline struvite staghorn calculi
qs.e: Bilateral partial obstruction classically presents early with an inability to concentrate urine, manifesting as polyuria and nocturia. Complete bilateral obstruction leads to oliguria or anuria.
